newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks weak, no recovery in sight.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks weak, no recovery in sight.

text.p: Croatian stocks continued a bearish trend on Thursday with leading issues sliding in line with a shaky performance of Croatian Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) in London. Market analysts predicting the trend would continue for some time.
"The market in general will be going down in the next month," said Nenad Pavletic, analyst at Auctor brokerage.

Market heavyweights, drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, accounted for most of the daily trade. Pliva lost 2.5 kuna and reached its support point, put by traders at 450 kuna, on volume of 3,914 shares.
"Pliva is hesitating in London...I think it is unstable and will slide in the long run on dwindling demand," Pavletic said. "It seems that market-makers in London are not supporting it."
Zagrebacka, Croatia's leading commercial bank, lost 40 kuna or two percent to 1,960 and was the day's most active stock with 6,123 shares sold.
Its preference stock - the E-series - gained 15 kuna to 1,175 on volume of 1,000 shares.
"The E-series is on the rise," Pavletic said, adding its price would continue up towards the bank's ordinary stock.
Eight of 15 active issues were down, four were up and three flat.
Turnover more than doubled to 15.7 million kuna.
Chocolate maker Kras, which dominated Wednesday's trade following the news of its increase in 1996 profit, lost 10 kuna to 410, with only 60 shares sold.
"Kras took a dip and it's a consequence of its inclusion in the (government-regulated) voucher privatisation list," Pavletic said.
The Croatian government has announced a mass privatisation scheme including dozens of companies it previously owned. Kras is one of the firms where the government has the largest stake.
Brewery Karlovacka Pivovara was the day's biggest gainer, adding 10 kuna or 3.3 percent to 310 from last week on volume of 100 shares.
The biggest decliner was shipper Jadroplov. It lost 65 kuna or 34 percent from last February to 125 on volume of 100 shares.
Two of four hotelier stocks were up and two down. Riviera Porec lost 12 kuna to 148 on volume of 128 shares and Istraturist added 5 kuna to 190, with 65 shares sold.
